---
title: "Iterative PCA imputation"
---

The [complete-case analysis](complete-case-analysis.qmd) discarded a Hillenbrand token whenever one of five steady measurements was unavailable. We now retain the tokens and ask whether the other acoustic measurements predict an unavailable formant estimate. The result is a prediction of a released acoustic cell, not a recovered observation from the recording.

[**Iterative PCA imputation**](https://search.r-project.org/CRAN/refmans/missMDA/html/imputePCA.html) repeatedly uses a rank-$K$ reconstruction to update missing cells while returning observed cells to their measured values. Principal components and matrix reconstruction have already been introduced; the new object is the update procedure.

We derive and implement that update, choose rank with registered artificial masks, predict the naturally missing cells, and then distinguish those predictions from recovered measurements.

::: {.callout-note title="Prerequisite: low-rank reconstruction"}
Review [centering and scaling](../factorization/centering-and-scaling.qmd), [principal component analysis](../factorization/principal-component-analysis.qmd), and [rank-$K$ reconstruction](../factorization/reconstruction.qmd). The treatment of [choosing the number of components](../factorization/choosing-components.qmd) supplies the holdout logic used below.
:::

## Constructing the acoustic matrix

The source and measurement process are introduced on the [preceding page](complete-case-analysis.qmd). We use the full continuous acoustic matrix: duration, F0, and the steady plus contour samples for F1--F3.

```{r}
#| label: load-hillenbrand-pca
#| message: false
#| warning: false

hill <- utils::read.csv(
  "data/hillenbrand-raw/hillenbrand-raw-formants.csv",
  check.names = FALSE
)

acoustic_columns <- c(
  "duration_ms",
  "f0_hz",
  grep(
    "^f[123]_(steady|time[1-8])_hz$",
    names(hill),
    value = TRUE
  )
)
acoustic_matrix <- as.matrix(hill[acoustic_columns])
storage.mode(acoustic_matrix) <- "double"

fallible_columns <- acoustic_columns[
  colSums(is.na(acoustic_matrix)) > 0L
]

stopifnot(
  nrow(acoustic_matrix) == 1668L,
  ncol(acoustic_matrix) == 29L,
  length(fallible_columns) == 14L,
  sum(is.na(acoustic_matrix)) == 379L,
  all(grepl("^f[23]_", fallible_columns))
)
```

The matrix has `r format(nrow(acoustic_matrix), big.mark = ",")` token rows and `r ncol(acoustic_matrix)` acoustic columns. Its `r sum(is.na(acoustic_matrix))` naturally missing cells occur in `r length(fallible_columns)` F2 or F3 columns. Duration, F0, and all F1 columns are complete.

## Defining the standardized update

Let $\mathbf{Y}$ be the incomplete acoustic matrix and let $M$ contain the cells treated as missing in a particular fit. Each fit estimates a center $\widehat\mu_j$ and scale $\widehat s_j$ from its observed training cells, then forms

$$
Z_{ij}=\frac{Y_{ij}-\widehat\mu_j}{\widehat s_j}
$$

where $Y_{ij}$ is available. Missing standardized cells begin at zero, which is the training-column mean after standardization. At iteration $t$, the rank-$K$ reconstruction is

$$
\widehat{\mathbf Z}^{(t)}_K
=\mathbf U^{(t)}_K\mathbf D^{(t)}_K
\mathbf V_K^{(t)\mathsf T}.
$$

One update is

$$
Z_{ij}^{(t+1)}=
\begin{cases}
Z_{ij} & \text{if }(i,j)\notin M,\\
\widehat Z_{K,ij}^{(t)} & \text{if }(i,j)\in M.
\end{cases}
$$

Thus only the missing cells change. We stop when their relative squared change is below $10^{-6}$,

$$
\frac{
  \sum_{(i,j)\in M}
  \left(Z_{ij}^{(t+1)}-Z_{ij}^{(t)}\right)^2
}{
  \max\left\{
    \sum_{(i,j)\in M}\left(Z_{ij}^{(t)}\right)^2,
    \epsilon_{\mathrm{machine}}
  \right\}
}<10^{-6},
$$

or after 1,000 iterations. The machine-precision floor makes the first comparison defined when every initialized missing cell is zero, exactly matching `max(..., .Machine$double.eps)` in the code.

The update is easier to see in a two-step trace. The following small matrix is already on a standardized scale; only its upper-right cell is missing. Rank one compresses the currently completed matrix, then the algorithm copies just that cell back into the next completed matrix.

```{r}
#| label: trace-two-pca-updates

toy <- matrix(c(1, NA, 0, 0, -1, 1), nrow = 3, byrow = TRUE) # dqr-allow: algorithm-setting
toy_missing <- is.na(toy)
toy_filled <- toy
toy_filled[toy_missing] <- 0

toy_trace <- numeric(2)
for (iteration in 1:2) {
  toy_svd <- base::svd(toy_filled, nu = 1, nv = 1)
  toy_rank_one <- toy_svd$u %*%
    matrix(toy_svd$d[1], 1, 1) %*%
    t(toy_svd$v)
  toy_filled[toy_missing] <- toy_rank_one[toy_missing]
  toy_trace[iteration] <- toy_filled[toy_missing]
}

data.frame(iteration = 0:2, imputed_z = c(0, toy_trace))
```

The printed values connect the recurrence to its implementation: iteration 0 is mean initialization, iteration 1 is the first rank-one prediction, and iteration 2 recomputes the singular vectors after inserting that prediction. A different initialization can lead to a different fixed point when the low-rank objective is nonconvex, so convergence from this initialization is an algorithmic fact rather than a uniqueness guarantee.

## Implementing the algorithm in base R

The function returns the completed matrix, training centers and scales, and convergence diagnostics. Rank zero is the training-column-mean reference.

```{r}
#| label: define-pca-imputation

pca_impute <- function(
  x,
  rank,
  tolerance = 1e-6,
  max_iterations = 1000L
) {
  x <- as.matrix(x)
  storage.mode(x) <- "double"
  missing <- is.na(x)

  center <- colMeans(x, na.rm = TRUE)
  scale <- vapply(
    seq_len(ncol(x)),
    function(column) stats::sd(x[, column], na.rm = TRUE),
    numeric(1)
  )

  stopifnot(
    all(is.finite(center)),
    all(is.finite(scale)),
    all(scale > 0)
  )

  standardized <- sweep(
    sweep(x, 2, center, FUN = "-"),
    2, scale, FUN = "/"
  )
  filled <- standardized
  filled[missing] <- 0

  if (rank == 0L) {
    reconstructed <- filled
    iterations <- 0L
    final_change <- 0
  } else {
    final_change <- Inf
    for (iteration in seq_len(max_iterations)) {
      decomposition <- base::svd(
        filled,
        nu = rank,
        nv = rank
      )
      reconstructed <- decomposition$u %*%
        diag(decomposition$d[seq_len(rank)], nrow = rank) %*%
        t(decomposition$v)

      updated <- filled
      updated[missing] <- reconstructed[missing]
      final_change <-
        sum((updated[missing] - filled[missing])^2) /
        max(sum(filled[missing]^2), .Machine$double.eps)
      filled <- updated

      if (final_change < tolerance) {
        break
      }
    }
    iterations <- iteration
    reconstructed <- filled
  }

  completed <- sweep(
    sweep(reconstructed, 2, scale, FUN = "*"),
    2, center, FUN = "+"
  )
  completed[!missing] <- x[!missing]

  list(
    completed = completed,
    center = center,
    scale = scale,
    iterations = iterations,
    final_change = final_change,
    converged = final_change < tolerance || rank == 0L
  )
}
```

The code estimates $\widehat\mu_j$ and $\widehat s_j$ before filling cells. A masked target thus cannot affect its own center or scale.

The default tolerance $10^{-6}$ asks the missing-cell update to change by less than roughly one part per million on the squared standardized scale. The cap of 1,000 iterations prevents an indefinitely running fit. Neither number follows from the Hillenbrand measurement process; they are numerical settings, so every reported fit checks `converged`, `iterations`, and `final_change`. Tightening the tolerance or changing the initialization is a useful sensitivity check when a substantive result depends on the completed cells.

## Choosing rank with registered masks

The number of retained components controls which relations can inform a missing cell. We compare $K\in\{0,1,2,3,4,5,8,10,12,15,20\}$ using eight registered validation masks. Each mask hides 5% of the naturally observed cells in every fallible column. Four smaller test masks are created afterward; their union is removed from every validation fit, so rank choice cannot use any test target directly or through preprocessing.

The rank grid includes the mean-only baseline, every small rank through five, and increasingly flexible reconstructions up to 20 of the 29 columns. Eight masks reduce dependence on one random split while keeping each fit large enough to estimate centers, scales, and component directions. The 5% validation fraction supplies enough targets to compare ranks; the four 1.25% test masks reserve disjoint cells without consuming the available table. These are design choices, not universal defaults, and the next page reports what target they validate. <!-- dqr-allow: algorithm-setting -->

```{r}
#| label: build-hillenbrand-validation-masks

make_mask <- function(
  data_matrix,
  eligible_columns,
  fraction,
  seed,
  excluded = matrix(
    FALSE,
    nrow(data_matrix),
    ncol(data_matrix)
  )
) {
  set.seed(seed)
  mask <- matrix(
    FALSE,
    nrow(data_matrix),
    ncol(data_matrix),
    dimnames = dimnames(data_matrix)
  )

  for (column_name in eligible_columns) {
    column <- match(column_name, colnames(data_matrix))
    observed_rows <- which(!is.na(data_matrix[, column]))
    available_rows <- observed_rows[
      !excluded[observed_rows, column]
    ]
    n_mask <- max(1L, floor(fraction * length(observed_rows)))
    selected_rows <- sample(
      available_rows,
      n_mask,
      replace = FALSE
    )
    mask[selected_rows, column] <- TRUE
  }

  mask
}

validation_repeats <- 8L
test_repeats <- 4L
mask_seeds <- 20261018L +
  seq_len(validation_repeats + test_repeats) - 1L

masks <- vector("list", length(mask_seeds))
used_cells <- matrix(
  FALSE,
  nrow(acoustic_matrix),
  ncol(acoustic_matrix),
  dimnames = dimnames(acoustic_matrix)
)

for (replicate in seq_along(masks)) {
  fraction <- if (replicate <= validation_repeats) {
    0.05
  } else {
    0.0125
  }
  masks[[replicate]] <- make_mask(
    acoustic_matrix,
    fallible_columns,
    fraction,
    mask_seeds[replicate],
    excluded = used_cells
  )
  used_cells <- used_cells | masks[[replicate]]
}

test_union <- Reduce(
  `|`,
  masks[validation_repeats + seq_len(test_repeats)]
)

stopifnot(
  all(!is.na(acoustic_matrix[used_cells])),
  max(Reduce(`+`, lapply(masks, as.integer))) == 1L
)
```

The masks are generated sequentially, so no cell appears in more than one. The following function scores only a validation mask, after also removing the entire test union.

```{r}
#| label: select-hillenbrand-pca-rank

score_validation <- function(rank, replicate) {
  artificial_mask <- masks[[replicate]]
  training <- acoustic_matrix
  training[artificial_mask] <- NA_real_
  training[test_union] <- NA_real_

  fit <- pca_impute(training, rank = rank)
  location <- which(artificial_mask, arr.ind = TRUE)
  truth <- acoustic_matrix[location]
  prediction <- fit$completed[location]
  training_scale <- fit$scale[location[, "col"]]

  data.frame(
    rank = rank,
    replicate = replicate,
    squared_standardized_error =
      ((prediction - truth) / training_scale)^2,
    converged = fit$converged
  )
}

candidate_ranks <- c(
  0L, 1L, 2L, 3L, 4L, 5L, 8L, 10L, 12L, 15L, 20L
)

validation_predictions <- do.call(
  rbind,
  lapply(candidate_ranks, function(rank) {
    do.call(
      rbind,
      lapply(seq_len(validation_repeats), function(replicate) {
        score_validation(rank, replicate)
      })
    )
  })
)

rank_curve <- stats::aggregate(
  squared_standardized_error ~ rank,
  validation_predictions,
  function(x) sqrt(mean(x))
)
names(rank_curve)[2] <- "standardized_rmse"
rank_curve$selected <- with(
  rank_curve,
  standardized_rmse == min(standardized_rmse)
)
selected_rank <- rank_curve$rank[rank_curve$selected][1]

stopifnot(
  all(validation_predictions$converged),
  selected_rank == 10L
)

rank_curve
```

```{r}
#| label: plot-hillenbrand-pca-rank
#| fig-width: 6.2
#| fig-height: 3.8

ggplot2::ggplot(
  rank_curve,
  ggplot2::aes(rank, standardized_rmse)
) +
  ggplot2::geom_line(color = "grey35", linewidth = 0.8) +
  ggplot2::geom_point(color = "grey35", size = 2) +
  ggplot2::geom_point(
    data = subset(rank_curve, selected),
    color = "#2B6F8A",
    size = 3
  ) +
  ggplot2::scale_x_continuous(breaks = candidate_ranks) +
  ggplot2::labs(
    x = "PCA rank",
    y = "Validation RMSE (training-standardized units)"
  ) +
  ggplot2::theme_classic(base_size = 11)
```

Rank `r selected_rank` has the lowest validation RMSE, `r sprintf("%.3f", min(rank_curve$standardized_rmse))`. The curve falls from `r sprintf("%.3f", rank_curve$standardized_rmse[rank_curve$rank == 0L])` at rank zero before rising again beyond the selected rank. This selection uses only validation targets; the [next page](validating-imputation.qmd) evaluates the choice on the untouched test masks.

## Predicting the naturally missing cells

After rank selection, we fit rank `r selected_rank` to the original matrix. Observed cells are copied back exactly. The remaining values are labeled predictions.

```{r}
#| label: predict-hillenbrand-natural-missingness

final_fit <- pca_impute(
  acoustic_matrix,
  rank = selected_rank
)

natural_location <- which(
  is.na(acoustic_matrix),
  arr.ind = TRUE
)

natural_predictions <- data.frame(
  token_id = hill$token_id[natural_location[, "row"]],
  vowel = hill$vowel[natural_location[, "row"]],
  measurement = colnames(acoustic_matrix)[natural_location[, "col"]],
  predicted_value_hz = final_fit$completed[natural_location],
  observed = FALSE,
  selected_rank = selected_rank
)

natural_prediction_summary <- stats::aggregate(
  predicted_value_hz ~ measurement,
  natural_predictions,
  function(x) c(
    cells = length(x),
    minimum = min(x),
    median = stats::median(x),
    maximum = max(x)
  )
)
natural_prediction_summary <- data.frame(
  measurement = natural_prediction_summary$measurement,
  natural_prediction_summary$predicted_value_hz,
  row.names = NULL,
  check.names = FALSE
)

stopifnot(
  final_fit$converged,
  all(final_fit$completed[!is.na(acoustic_matrix)] ==
    acoustic_matrix[!is.na(acoustic_matrix)]),
  nrow(natural_predictions) == 379L,
  all(!natural_predictions$observed)
)

natural_prediction_summary
```

The final fit supplies predictions for all `r nrow(natural_predictions)` natural omissions. The table deliberately calls them `predicted_value_hz`; there is no observed target against which to calculate their error.

## Imputed values remain estimates

A completed matrix may look indistinguishable from an observed matrix in software. The two kinds of cells are not epistemically equivalent. An observed cell contains an estimate obtained from the recorded signal. An imputed cell contains a prediction under a linear low-rank assumption, training centers and scales, the selected rank, and an initialization rule.

Using one completed matrix in a later analysis treats these predictions as fixed and may understate the uncertainty created by the missing measurements. A procedure that propagates imputation uncertainty requires more machinery than this single reconstruction. The completed data should thus retain the observation indicator.

The procedure is also **transductive**: it learns the component directions from the same set of tokens whose isolated cells it completes. It is appropriate for filling cells in this released matrix under its observed-column structure. It is not, without a separate out-of-sample construction, a rule for predicting an entirely new speaker or token.

PCA imputation may also pull unusual but real measurements toward the leading linear components. A rare vowel category, a nonlinear acoustic relation, or an extreme value can be reconstructed poorly even when the algorithm converges. Numerical convergence diagnoses the update, not the substantive adequacy of the low-rank representation.

## Checking the reconstruction

1. Which cells may change after each rank-$K$ reconstruction?
2. Where are the centers and scales estimated in the validation procedure?
3. Why is rank zero a column-mean reference on the standardized scale?
4. What does the final fit establish about the `r nrow(natural_predictions)` natural omissions, and what remains unknown?

**Answers.** (1) Only cells in $M$ may change; observed entries are copied back after every reconstruction. (2) Centers and scales are estimated from the cells left in each training matrix. (3) Rank zero reconstructs standardized missing cells as zero, which back-transforms to the training-column mean. (4) The fit supplies model-based predictions and numerical convergence diagnostics; the true missing values, their errors, and imputation uncertainty remain unknown.

Iterative PCA imputation alternates between rank-$K$ reconstruction and replacement of cells treated as missing. It preserves observed cells, but its predictions depend on a low-rank model and a validation-selected component count. We next test that selected procedure by [masking values that were actually observed](validating-imputation.qmd).

## Recap

1. Standardization places the acoustic columns on comparable scales, and every preprocessing quantity is estimated from training cells.
2. Each iteration reconstructs the completed matrix at rank $K$ but updates only the cells declared missing.
3. The epsilon floor, tolerance, iteration cap, and initialization define a reproducible numerical algorithm without guaranteeing a unique substantive solution.
4. Registered validation masks choose rank; the [validation-error section](validating-imputation.qmd#defining-the-validation-error) next separates that choice from the final test.
